data.narrative:
Cartesia is a Series B-stage AI & Software company that has raised $186M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Palantir), with four direct same-sector, same-stage peers: Scale AI ($29.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), and Field AI ($2.0B).

Two triangulation methods anchor this analysis. The stage-progression approach applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $186M total raised, yielding $353M. The peer-median method directly benchmarks against the four same-stage AI & Software comparables, producing a $4.4B implied valuation (range: $2.0B–$29.0B). The peer set exhibits wide dispersion; Scale AI's $29.0B represents an outlier, while the interquartile range clusters between $2.0B and $5.6B.

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated range of $300M (low) to $5.1B (high), with a median of $2.4B. The stage-progression floor reflects conservative capital-based reasoning, while peer median better captures market pricing for comparable-stage frontier AI. Key uncertainties include: Cartesia's specific revenue run-rate and growth trajectory relative to peers; whether Scale AI's valuation represents a market precedent or sector outlier; and the stability of AI infrastructure valuations amid evolving demand. The wide peer range ($2.0B–$29.0B) signals material model sensitivity to peer selection and stage definition.
